terms.meaning: A line that cuts a segment into two equal parts and is at 90° to it.
A line that cuts an angle into two equal angles.
A 6-sided figure with equal sides and equal angles.
Covering a region using a set of shapes, without gaps or overlaps.

items.name: Equal distances from two points
items.formula: Such points lie on the perpendicular bisector
items.example: If AX = AY and BX = BY, then line AB is the perpendicular bisector of XY.

items.name: A 90° angle
items.formula: Draw the perpendicular bisector of a segment
items.example: It meets the segment at 90° at its midpoint.

items.name: A 60° angle
items.example: Each angle is 60°, and 180° − 60° = 120° on a straight line.

items.name: A line through a point, parallel to another
items.formula: Copy an angle to make equal corresponding angles
items.example: Equal corresponding angles make the lines parallel.

items.name: Regular hexagon from triangles
items.formula: Six equilateral triangles around a point

items.name: Grid with 2 × 1 tiles
items.formula: An m × n grid can be tiled only if m × n is even
items.example: 5 × 3 has 15 squares, so it cannot be tiled. 4 × 3 has 12, so it can.

items.name: Colouring a grid
items.formula: Each 2 × 1 tile covers 1 black and 1 white square
items.example: A region with 8 black and 6 white squares cannot be tiled, even with 14 squares.

items.name: Regular polygons that tile the plane

mistakes.text: An even number of squares is not enough for tiling with 2 × 1 tiles. The black and white counts must also match.
Regular pentagons cannot tile the plane. Their 108° angles do not fit around a point: 3 × 108° = 324°.
For a perpendicular bisector, use the same compass radius from both ends, and make it more than half the segment.
